sections.section_title: The Scourging and the Mock Enthronement
sections.summary: The neutral reading presents the scourging and mock coronation as the world's attempt to ridicule the kingship that the document has affirmed since the prologue.
The neutral reading presents Pilate's 'Behold, the Man!' and the chief priests' demand for crucifixion, with the legal charge that Jesus 'made himself out to be the Son of God.'

The neutral reading presents Jesus's assertion that Pilate's authority is 'given from above' -- the sovereign God who gave authority to the Son (17:2) also governs the authority of the political rulers who execute him.

sections.section_title: The Final Exchange and the Handover
sections.summary: The neutral reading presents the crowd's 'We have no king but Caesar' as Israel's leaders formally renouncing the kingship of God in favor of Rome's, the climactic act of rejection.
The neutral reading presents the crucifixion with the restrained narrative typical of the author, focusing on Jesus carrying his own cross to Golgotha.

The neutral reading presents the trilingual inscription 'Jesus the Nazarene, the King of the Jews' as the ironic proclamation of truth by the one who asked 'What is truth?' -- Pilate unwittingly announces to all nations what the document has been arguing.
The neutral reading presents the division of garments as the fulfillment of Psalm 22:18, with the seamless tunic possibly evoking the high priest's robe.

sections.section_title: The Mother and the Beloved Disciple
sections.summary: The neutral reading presents Jesus's creation of a new family at the cross, entrusting his mother to the beloved disciple -- the community of the cross replaces biological kinship with a family constituted by Jesus's word.

The neutral reading presents 'It is finished' (tetelestai) as the declaration that the work the Father gave Jesus to do (4:34, 17:4) is now completed, with Jesus voluntarily giving up his spirit rather than having it taken.

sections.section_title: The Unbroken Bones and the Pierced Side
sections.summary: The neutral reading presents the blood and water from the pierced side as connecting to the document's themes of sacrificial blood (6:53-56) and living water as the Spirit (7:37-39), with the Passover lamb identification (unbroken bones fulfilling Exodus 12:46) and the eyewitness testimony as the most emphatic truth-claim in the document.

The neutral reading presents the burial by Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus -- both formerly hidden believers now acting publicly -- as demonstrating the cross's power to bring concealed faith into the open.
